Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

sī

conjunction: the indicative for a real condition, the present or perfect subjunctive for a supposed one, the imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive for one contrary to fact

if; if you agree, if you like: the polite way to put a suggestion; whether, to see if

In this lexicon

  • if

    the recommended word · classical · Hor. S. 2.6.39: sī vīs, potes; Cato Agr. 1.7: sī mē rogābis, sīc dīcam

  • suggest

    also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.23: nunc, sī vidētur, hoc, illud aliās; Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.7: sī tibi vidētur

  • whether

    also used · classical · Petr. 33.2: temptēmus tamen, sī adhūc sorbilia sunt; Phaedr. 4.8.3–4: haec cum temptāret sī qua rēs esset cibī

  • sī ita est: case

    classical

  • sī modo: condition

    classical

  • quod sī (quodsī): if

    classical

  • sī nōn: if not

    classical

  • sī minus: if not

    classical

  • quid sī …?: suppose

    classical

  • sī vīs, potes

    if you want to, you canHor. S. 2.6.39

    What is needed is twice welcome if you offer it unasked.Publ. B 1
